title: Lesson 1: Noticing and Wondering: Observing and Asking Questions about the Sun, Moon, and Stars
objective: Students will observe and describe patterns in pictures and videos of the sun, moon, and stars, and ask and record questions about their observations.

what_is_taught.skill: describe observations in pictures and videos
record observations and questions in shared writing
identify and discuss vocabulary related to astronomy and patterns
participate in partner discussions using sentence frames
use classroom discussion protocols (Picture Tea Party, Think-Pair-Share)

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify and recognize vocabulary and patterns in pictures and text
student_actions.oral_production: share observations and questions orally with partners and whole group
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain reasoning for word associations and observations during discussions
student_actions.comprehension_response: respond to questions about the text and illustrations orally and in partner talk, using evidence from the text and observations to support answers and ideas, sometimes using sentence frames for support and elaboration, and contribute ideas to anchor charts and word walls to build understanding and vocabulary related to astronomy and patterns in the sky

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model fluent, expressive read-alouds of texts about the sun, moon, and stars; model use of vocabulary words and anchor charts; demonstrate classroom discussion protocols (Picture Tea Party, Think-Pair-Share).
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What are some things that Elvin wondered about?
What word does the word astronomer remind you of?
What is Elvin wondering about now?
What did you notice in your pictures?
What does the word pattern mean?
Why do you think the astronomer gave Elvin photographs of patterns when Elvin was wondering if there were facts about the sun, moon, and stars?
What is a pattern that the sun follows?
What, in the text, makes you think so?
Where is the horizon line in the illustration on page 8?

What are new questions or wonders you have about the sun?

scope.breadth: observing and describing patterns in the sun, moon, and stars; asking and recording questions about observations
scope.depth: using multiple texts, photographs, videos, and discussion protocols to build understanding and vocabulary

context.stimulus_provided: texts, photographs, videos, anchor charts, word walls

sections_covered.warm_up: Reading Aloud: 'Elvin, the Boy Who Loved the Sky,' Part 5
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Focused Read-aloud: Does the Sun Sleep?: Noticing Sun, Moon, and Star Patterns, Pages 4-9
sections_covered.guided_practice: Picture Tea Party: Pattern Photographs; Engaging the Scientist: 'Observe Sunrise and Sunset'
sections_covered.independent_application: Shared Writing: Recording Our Observations and Questions about the Sun, Moon, and Stars
sections_covered.check_for_understanding: Equity sticks cold calling and total participation techniques during discussions
sections_covered.differentiated_reinforce: ELL supports including partner modeling, sentence frames, and physical seating options
sections_covered.differentiated_extend: Encouraging students to add on to others' ideas using sentence frames

supports.english_language_learners: Provides partner talk, sentence frames, repeated readings, visual supports, and modeling of protocols to support ELLs.
supports.universal_design_udl: Offers physical seating options for sensory needs, multiple modes of engagement (listening, speaking, viewing), and scaffolded discussion protocols.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Uses sentence frames and partner modeling to support comprehension and oral language production.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourages students to add on to others' ideas and provide reasoning during discussions.

assessment.method: Observation of student participation in discussions, partner talks, and shared writing contributions

notes: The lesson integrates multiple modalities including read-alouds, visual pattern photographs, videos, and interactive discussion protocols to build comprehension and vocabulary about astronomy and patterns in the sky. Equity sticks are used to ensure equitable participation. Supports for ELLs and students with sensory needs are embedded.
